title: Price validation and tax calculation in cart.ts

sections.title: Subtotal validation and calculation
sections.prose: The `subtotal` function takes an array of prices, validates every entry, and returns their arithmetic sum. The reduction starts at zero. A non-finite or negative entry follows an explicit `RangeError` path. The visible body reads the array to validate and sum it; it shows no explicit mutation or external call.
sections.spokenText: This function checks every price, then adds the values together starting from zero. It returns their subtotal as a number.

claims.prose: `subtotal` is the price-array operation in this file: its signature accepts `prices` and declares a numeric return.
`subtotal` sums `prices` with `reduce`, starting the accumulator at zero and adding each value before returning.
A non-finite or negative item in `prices` makes the validation condition true, and `RangeError` is thrown with a message describing the accepted values.

claims.prose: The visible `subtotal` body checks and reduces `prices` and returns a number; it contains no explicit write to the input or external call.
claims.inferenceBasis: This conclusion is limited to the complete visible function body, which shows array checks, a reduction, and a return.

sections.title: Tax-adjusted total
sections.prose: `totalWithTax` accepts prices and a tax rate. It rejects a non-finite or negative tax rate before invoking `subtotal`, then returns the subtotal multiplied by one plus the rate. If price validation throws inside `subtotal`, the visible `totalWithTax` body has no local catch.
sections.spokenText: The function checks the tax rate first. If it passes, the subtotal is adjusted by applying a multiplier of one plus the rate. An invalid tax rate raises an error before that calculation.

claims.prose: `totalWithTax` handles a `prices` array and `taxRate`, and its declared output is a number.
